title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Tuvalu: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Tuvalu: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for Tuvalu: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml: When a death occurs in Tuvalu, practical mortuary constraints require rapid medical certification and burial coordination alongside formal registration and benefit claims. Because domestic ministry portals provide limited online administrative guidance, this checklist relies on verified Tuvalu National Provident Fund (TNPF) statutory pages, Tuvalu statutory texts, and accredited regional diplomatic and consular guidance [1][4][6][8][9][11].

steps.title: Immediate medical certification, 24-hour mortuary reality, and burial rules
steps.html:
• Contact emergency dispatch on 911 (for medical, police, and fire) if death occurs outside medical care, or liaise directly with Princess Margaret Hospital in Funafuti (+688 20765), where the attending hospital doctor and Director of Health issue the medical Death Certificate [9][10].
  • Coordinate burial immediately: diplomatic consular reports record that Tuvalu has no formal funeral homes, no cremation facilities, and a hospital mortuary relying solely on formalin without adequate refrigeration, meaning burial typically occurs within 24 hours [9].
  • Confirm land and casket arrangements immediately, because Tuvalu has no designated public cemetery (meaning landowner permission is required for burial) and no lead-lined caskets, making overseas shipment of remains impracticable [9].

steps.title: Civil death registration under the Births, Deaths and Marriages Registration Act
steps.html:
• Register the death under the Births, Deaths and Marriages Registration Act (Cap. 17.10) through the Birth Registry Office (Funafuti) or, on outer islands, through the Local Government Council (Kaupule), which forwards civil registration records annually to Funafuti [6][8][11].
  • Under published UK consular profile documentation on Tuvalu's civil registry framework, deaths must be registered within 12 months of the date of death [11].
  • Request multiple certified Death Certificate extracts promptly for Tuvalu National Provident Fund (TNPF) claims, bank closures, court filings, and any overseas consular reporting [1][11][12].

steps.title: Tuvalu National Provident Fund (TNPF) death benefit and nomination rules
steps.html:
• Notify Tuvalu National Provident Fund (TNPF) at its Vaiaku, Funafuti headquarters (P.O. Box 51, Vaiaku, Funafuti; Tel +688 20983 / +688 20693 / +688 20698; Monday to Friday 9:00 AM to 1:30 PM) or through the relevant outer-island Kaupule office listed on TNPF's office hours schedule [1][2][3][4].
  • Submit the TNPF Death Benefit application along with the AUD$ 20 application fee, official Death Certificate, claimant identity documents, and beneficiary proofs [1][5].
  • Where a deceased member left no valid nomination or an invalid nomination, TNPF refers estate distribution under the Tuvalu National Provident Fund Act to the Lands Department and the Lands Court [1].

steps.title: Probate, Lands Court native estates, Attorney General, and tax status
steps.html:
• Distinguish formal personal property from native estate and customary land assets: non-customary estate grants (Probate or Letters of Administration) proceed through the High Court of Tuvalu, whereas native estates, customary land succession, and customary wills are governed by island Lands Courts and Lands Officers under the Native Lands Act and Administration of Native Estates Regulations [1]. Confirm statutory filing requirements or legislative texts through Office of the Attorney General (+688 20823) [4][9].
  • Request unpaid wages or final leave settlement from the deceased worker's employer under the Labour and Employment Relations Act 2017 (or public service conditions for civil servants), and close personal tax obligations with domestic revenue authorities; Tuvalu does not impose a separate inheritance or estate tax [7].

steps.title: Consular legalisation and notifying banks and institutions
steps.html:
• Because Tuvalu is not a Contracting Party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention, certified Tuvalu Death Certificates and court grants required by foreign banks, insurers, or registries need diplomatic or consular legalisation rather than a Hague Apostille [13]. Foreign nationals' families may also contact their accredited diplomatic mission (such as U.S. Embassy Suva regional consular guidance covering Tuvalu) to document a death abroad [12].
  • Notify domestic banks, employers, utility offices, and Kaupule registries in writing using certified Death Certificate extracts [4][11].
  • Retain complete copies of hospital certificates, Birth Registry receipts, TNPF acknowledgements, and Lands Court or High Court orders [1][9][11].

contacts.name: Princess Margaret Hospital
contacts.note: Primary hospital in Funafuti; attending doctor and Director of Health issue Death Certificates. National emergency dispatch: 911.

contacts.name: Birth Registry Office (Funafuti)
contacts.note: Central civil registry in Funafuti receiving local registrations (12-month statutory window) and annual returns from outer-island Kaupule.

contacts.name: Tuvalu National Provident Fund (TNPF)
contacts.note: Vaiaku, Funafuti (P.O. Box 51; +688 20983 / 20693 / 20698); AUD$ 20 Death Benefit application fee; refers missing nominations to Lands Dept/Lands Court.

contacts.name: Office of the Attorney General
contacts.note: Central government legal office providing statutory oversight in Funafuti (+688 20823).
